Bench: P.Madhavi Devi
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice P.Madhavi Devi
 Writ Petition No.37826 of 2022
 Order:

In this Writ Petition, petitioners are seeking a writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondents, more particularly the action of the respondents No.2 and 3 in interfering with the petitioners peaceful possession of the property i.e., the land admeasuring 3500 sq.yards in Revenue Sy.Nos.214/5 to 9 later assigned as Town Survey (TS) No.3/1, 3/2, 18 & 19 of Ward No.91, Block-D,
on the western portion adjacent to Greenland Guest House, situated at Khairthabad Village,
Golconda (now Khairthabad) Mandal, Hyderabad, through respondents No.4 and 5, as illegal,
arbitrary and contrary to the principles of natural justice and consequently to direct the respondents No.2 and 3 and their staff/employees, respondents No.4 and 5 not to interfere with the peaceful possession of the petitioners over the subject land and to pass such other order or orders.
2. Brief facts leading to the filing of the present writ petition are that the 1st petitioner claims to be the owner and possessor of 3500 sq.yards of land in Sy.Nos.214/5 to 9, later assigned as TS No.3/1,
3/2, 18 & 19 of Ward No.91, Block-D, on the western portion adjacent to Greenland Guest House,
situated at Khairthabad Village, Golconda (now Khairthabad) Mandal, Hyderabad and the 2nd petitioner claims to have entered into a registered Agreement of Sale dt.11.07.2022 vide PMD,J Document No.2123 of 2022 registered at S.R.O., S.R.Nagar for purchase of the subject property and also to have become the absolute owner and peaceful possessor of land admeasuring 300 sq.yards,
part of the property belonging to the 1st petitioner having purchased the same vide registered Sale Deed Document No.2124 of 2022 registered at Sub-Registrar Office, S.R.Nagar, dated 11.07.2022.
Thus, the 2nd petitioner claims to be the successor in title and interst of the 1st petitioner in respect of the subject property.
3. The brief history of the title of the 1st petitioner as claimed by her is as under:-
1st petitioner

's grandfather, Late Sri.Raja Kundan Lal has purchased 100 bighas of land in Sy.No.214/1 vide registered Sale Deed bearing No.32/31319 and since then,
the land in Sy.No.214/1 has been the 1st petitioner's family property.

Sri.Dwarakanath Kapoor and Smt.Jai Rani are the biological parents of the petitioner No.1 and Late Sri.Raja Karan Pershad and Smt.Brij Rani, the son and daughter- in-law of Raja Kundal Lal are the adopted parents of the 1st petitioner, and she was legally adopted on 09.04.1959.

The Civil Court dismissed the suit on 07.04.1961.
Aggrieved, Jitender Pershad filed an appeal in the High Court vide CCC Appeal PMD,J No.7 of 1962.
The said appeal was allowed by the High Court on 16.01.1967 granting 50% of the share in the property.
However, during the pendency of the appeal before the High Court, Sri.Jitender Pershad died on 02.02.1965 and his wife Smt.Kunwar Rani was brought on record as his legal heir.

4. Aggrieved by the appeal orders dt.16.01.1967, Late Sri.Raja Karan Pershad filed an appeal in the Hon'ble Apex Court vide C.A.No.1048 of 1967 and the same was partly allowed modifying the High Court's order i.e. modifying the share from 50% to 1/3rd.

5. Further, in the year 1970, Smt.Kunwar Rani filed O.S.No.115 of 1970 on the file of the Additional Chief Judge-cum-II Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, City civil Court, Hyderabad, claiming 50% of share in Smt.Brij Rani's property.

During his lifetime, Sri.Raja Karan Pershad had executed a registered Will Deed dt.13.08.1968 bequeathing his properties to the 1st petitioner herein.
Thus, 1st petitioner was brought on record as his legal heir.

6. After the death of Sri. Raja Karan Persad, the 1st petitioner, as his legal heir, filed an O.P.No.33 of 1974 on the file of the Hon'ble Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, against Smt.Kunwar Rani for grant of probate and same was allowed on 29.03.1979.

7. Aggrieved by the same, i.e., dismissal order dt.28.12.1981, Kunwar Rani filed a Special Leave Petition i.e., SLP.No.3151 of 1982 before the Hon'ble Apex Court.

During the pendency of the said SLP and O.S.No.115 of 1970, Sri.Dwarkanath Kapoor (1st petitioner's biological father) and Smt.Kunwar Rani have entered into a Memorandum of Compromise, as per the advice of well wishers and family friends, vide I.A.No.123 of 1978 in O.S.No.28 of 1959 i.e., the suit filed by late Jitender Pershad for partition of the property.

In view of the same, Smt.Kunwar Rani agreed to withdraw the SLP and accepted the Will and thereby the Probate proceedings have been effected and the Will was legalized and the 1st petitioner became the absolute and legitimate owner and possessor of the subject property.

The 1st petitioner immediately approached the High Court by filing the Writ Petition i.e., W.P.No.20093 of 1993 for restraining the respondents/State authorities from interfering with the physical possession and the construction of compound wall on the Western portion of the property.

On 28.12.1993, this Court disposed of the writ petition with a direction to the 1st petitioner to file a suit in the Civil Court and obtain necessary orders including injunction against the State authorities and directed the State authorities not to interfere with the property for two weeks thereafter.

13. In view of the Judgments of the Courts as stated above, the 1st petitioner claims to be the absolute owner and peaceful possessor of the subject property and approached the registration authorities to sell and register the property in favour of the 2nd petitioner.
However, without assigning any reason, the Sub-Registrar's office, S.R.Nagar, refused to receive and register the documents.

Therefore, the 1st petitioner filed W.P.No.26378 of 2021 and the same was disposed of by PMD,J this Court vide orders dt.22.10.2021 directing the Registering authority to receive and register the documents relating to the subject property.

In compliance of the directions of this Court,
the Registering authority registered the Agreement of Sale dt.11.07.2022 vide Document No.2123 of 2022, executed by the1st petitioner in favour of the 2nd petitioner along with Sale Deed dt.11.07.2022 vide Document No.2124 of 2022.
Thus, the 2nd petitioner has become the Agreement of Sale holder in respect of the subject property and absolute owner in respect of 300 sq.yards of the subject property.

14. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the 2nd petitioner is claiming to be the owner of the property and it is alleged that when he went to the property, he was prevented to enter the same by the staff of the 3rd & 4th respondents stating that the property belonged to the State Government and not the petitioners herein.
Aggrieved by the said action of the respondents, this writ petition has been filed.

15. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the above facts would go to show that the petitioner has been declared as the rightful and absolute owner and peaceful possessor of the subject property and the State authorities have miserably failed to prove their title over the subject property.

It is submitted that the subject property being the property of the PMD,J grandfather of the 1st petitioner, was under her possession all along and it is the State authorities who were trying to grab the property of the petitioner without any right or entitlement.

Therefore,
he seeks a direction from this Court to prevent the respondents from interfering with the peaceful possession of the petitioners over the subject property.

16. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that originally, the entire land in Survey No.214/1 (old) belonged only to the grandfather of the 1st petitioner i.e., Raja Kundan Lal and on the requisition from the Executive Engineer, P.W.D., Buildings Division No.2, the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition (General), Hyderabad District, proposed to acquire 23 Acres 8.6 gts., of land in Sy.No.214/1 of Kundan Bagh in Khairthabad Village for the purpose of construction of residential quarters for Secretaries of the Government of the then State of Andhra Pradesh and Deputy Secretaries and accordingly notification and declaration were published in this regard under Sections 4(1) & 6 of the Land Acquisition Act in the A.P.Government Gazette dt.30.11.1961 and 11.01.1962 respectively.

It is submitted that Land Acquisition Officer (LAO), after enquiry under Section 11 of the LA Act, delivered an award dt.24.06.1964 in which the cost of the land was assessed at Rs.4.50 paisa per square yard and the compensation was fixed at Rs.5,05,620/-, cost of the trees standing on the land at Rs.2,260/- and solatium of Rs.76,182/-, PMD,J thereby arriving at a total amount of Rs.5,84,062/- towards its market value and this was fixed as the compensation amount.

It is submitted that in view of the finding of the Hon'ble High Court in CCCA.No.7 of 1962, the Civil Court held that late Sri.Jitender Pershad was entitled to half share of the compensation amount which was deposited into the Court for the property in Sy.No.214/1 i.e., 23 Acres 8.6 gts., acquired by the Government.

17. The learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that before the Land Acquisition proceedings in the year 1964, the extent of land in Sy.No.214/1 was Ac.30-34gts., and after the Land Acquisition proceedings, the unacquired land in Sy.No.214/1 was Ac.7.25 gts., or 37,686 sq.yards and further the Sy.No.214/1 was PMD,J sub-divided into Sy.Nos.214/4 to 9.
Later the mentioned survey numbers were reassigned or correlated with the T.S.Nos.3/1, 3/2 & 18 respectively.

It is submitted that out of the unacquired Ac.7.25 gts., or 37,686 sq.yards, an extent of 880 sq.yards was acquired by the then Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad for the purpose of flyover in the year 1982-83 and an extent of 19168 sq.yards i.e., almost 4 Acres was sold by the 1st petitioner to Sri.Lakshmi Prasad Agarwal and others vide Sale Deed Document No.1948 of 2000.

It is submitted that an Agreement of Sale for 3500 sq.yards was executed by the 1st petitioner in favour of the 2nd petitioner and an extent of 907 sq.yards was gifted by the 1st petitioner to her husband vide Gift Deed Document No.2205 of 2022 and balance land of 13,231 sq.yards is in encroachments including the encroachments made by the 3rd respondent, as observed by the Civil Court in the order in I.A.No.559 of 1998 in O.S.No.5143 of 1993 filed for amendment of prayer in the suit.

It is submitted that the 1st petitioner, therefore, has the clear and absolute title over the subject land and has proved the same through various documents in the Civil Court as well as the Special Court in the Land Grabbing Case, whereas the respondents have not produced any documents to show their title to the property, but are claiming the property by creating fabricated documents, in the guise of illegal survey.

He further submitted that the respondent had filed the L.G.C.No.152 of 1998 before the Special Court and have miserably failed to prove its title PMD,J over the property and under Section 8(6) of the A.P.Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982, the findings of the Special Court shall be binding and conclusive on all the persons having interest on such land and the said findings have become final as the petitioner therein failed to challenge the same.

He therefore, prayed that the writ petition be allowed ad the respondents be directed not to interfere with the petitioners'
possession of the property.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate General appearing for the respondents, vehemently supported the averments made in the counter affidavit and submitted that the subject property is the property of the State Government and the P.W.D., Department and that the petitioners herein are, in fact, encroachers of the subject property.

He also reiterated the averments made in the counter affidavit filed along with the stay vacate petition in I.A.No.2 of 2022, filed by the respondent No.2 on behalf of the respondents No.1 to 3.
20.

He took the preliminary objection that the writ petition is not maintainable under law or on facts as it is filed in a highly speculative manner and with oblique motive of grabbing the Government property, more particularly the vacant land appurtenant to Green Lands Guest House,
situated in T.S.No.19/P (old Sy.No.215) (2020) 9 SCC 356 2011 (6) ALD 145 (DB) 2017 (5) ALD 64 1997 (1) ALD 442 PMD,J of Khairatabad Village and Mandal, Hyderabad District.

It is submitted that the petitioners have no right, whatsoever, in the above property and thereby cannot seek adjudication of the cause espoused in the writ petition before this Court as disputed questions of facts are raised in the writ petition.
Therefore, he sought dismissal of the writ petition at the admission stage itself as not maintainable under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

21. He further submitted that the writ petition is also not maintainable for non-joinder of the Roads & Buildings Department, which has allotted the property to GAD for the State Guest House, as party respondent.

He submitted that the party likely to be affected by the relief claimed in the writ petition, if any, should be arrayed as party respondent or else the affected party will be deprived of defending his/its rights and in bringing to the notice of the Hon'ble Court the true facts.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate General further submitted that the writ petitioners have approached this Court with unclean hands and are trying to mislead this Court.

It is submitted that the Court cases referred to by the petitioners are all concerning the land forming part of the Sy.No.214/1 of Khairatabad Village, whereas the land belonging to respondents No.1 to 3 is in Sy.No.215 and therefore, there is conscious attempt of the petitioners in trying to create cloud over the PMD,J title with respect of the property belonging to the Government in Sy.No.215, new Sy.No.19/P.

He further submitted that the 1st petitioner executed a registered Agreement of Sale in favour of the 2nd petitioner in respect of the 3,500 sq.yards and also registered Sale deed on the same day i.e., on 11.07.2022, in respect of 300 sq.yards which show the anxiety of the petitioners to bring into existence the registered documents and thereby claiming title and possession of the property belonging to Roads & Buildings Department which was in the lawful possession of the respondents No.1 to 3.
Therefore, according to him those documents cannot be relied upon to come to any conclusion about the title and possession of the property by the writ petition.

23. Learned Advocate General further submitted that there is no cause of action for the petitioners against the respondents to seek relief in the writ petition in as much as there is no semblance of right, title or other interest, as the property referred to in Paras-1 & 2 of the writ affidavit, is having no relation to the property owned by the Roads & Buildings Department which is in the possession and presently in enjoyment of the respondents No.1 to 3.

It is submitted that the vacant land appurtenant thereto spanning into Ac.6.18gts., enclosed by compound wall which is in existence for the past more than 97 years i.e., little less than a century having been built in the year 1925.

It is further submitted that the respondents have nothing to do with the alleged purchase of land in Sy.No.214/1 by Sri.Raja Kundan Lal and PMD,J that the land which is in the lawful possession and enjoyment of the respondents namely Green Land Guest House, vacant land appurtenant thereto and staff quarters are in Sy.No.215 and T.S.No.19/P and therefore, the petitioners have no right whatsoever and possession over the land in Sy.No.215 and therefore, the writ petition is not maintainable against the respondents.

Learned Advocate General further submitted that the 1st petitioner filed W.P.No.20093 of 1993 against the respondents herein, against the alleged interference of the respondents and this Court had directed the petitioner to file appropriate suit before the Civil Court and obtain appropriate orders, including injunction.

It is submitted that despite of said directions of this Court, the 1st petitioner, though has filed a suit before the Civil Court and has sought amendment of prayer by claiming relief of declaration, the petitioner did not re- present the suit, but instead filed CRP i.e.,

It is submitted that LGC was filed by the MRO,
Khairathabad alleging that the 1st petitioner and other respondents in the LGC grabbed land in old Sy.No.214/1 and T.S.No.3/2, which has nothing to do with the dispute projected by the petitioners in the present writ petition.

(i) The petitioner denies each and every averment, allegation, contention and submissions contained in the counter affidavit, which is contrary to or inconsistent with what is stated by the petitioner and that he reserves to file further affidavit if need arises.

(ii) The writ petition is filed on true, accurate and actual facts and is absolutely maintainable by facts and law in view of the documents, judgments and decrees by the Hon'ble Courts in favour of the 1st petitioner whose flow of tile and possession undisputedly and unequivocally traces for more than a century and further also establishes that the 1st petitioner's property falls under Survey No.214 and not under T.S.No.19/P (old Survey No.215) as claimed by the respondents.

(iv) It is of paramount importance to note that Land Grabbing Court has ample jurisdiction and power to decide the title and possession vested under Section 7(1) and 7(A) of the Andhra Pradesh Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982 and it was decided in favour of the 1st petitioner vide judgment dated 04.10.2004 and the petitioner No.1 has been conferred undisputed title.

Thus,
dispute relating to the title and possession of the petitioner's property was resolved long ago and declared in favour of the 1st petitioner.

Every finding of the Special Court with regard to any alleged act of land grabbing shall be conclusive proof of the fact of land grabbing and of the persons who committed such land grabbing, and every judgment of the Special Court with regard to the determination of title and ownership to, or lawful possession of, any land grabbed shall be binding on all persons having interest in such land.
